uim4v1:250: The five layers are not a parallel checklist, but an optimization ladder where both ROI and fixed investment rise layer by layer. The usage-habit layer changes behavior, with almost zero infrastructure cost and immediate results; the model-routing layer requires a set of routing/budget infrastructure; the context-engineering layer calls for introducing a compression toolchain; the code-graph layer requires building a graph database and index; the agent-architecture layer requires reworking the entire task orchestration approach. Each layer precisely targets a different cost source — habits cure "meaningless history and wasted tokens", routing cures "expensive models doing cheap work", context engineering cures "repeatedly sending the same prefix", code graphs cure "searching for code from scratch every time", and agent architecture cures "stuffing every task into the same big context".
